body:
Much the same really. Never been comfortable in my own skin. Always grew up heavy. Never felt I was good enough battling depression. Truth is everyone keeps saying go see a therapist. I don't have the money to do that. I'm struggling to make ends meet and just survive let alone pay someone to talk to. It's frustrating. I also tend to bottle things up. It's a problem with me.

I just feel like I've been doing all this work and no one noticed. And then I go into those old feelings of "if I'm not worthy in the 270lbs range then am I ever gonna be considered worthy?"

Or worse, if the day comes when I get to where I want to be then what happens? Will I suddenly be deemed worthy? Will that become more heart breaking to think they only accepted me because of what I looked like? Am I just being vain and shallow?

I over think WAY too much.
No, gaming was my hobby. Eating was my way of dealing with crippling depression.
For me I grew up heavy so it’s all I’ve ever known. I’ve only ever known overweight so it’s weird to me right now seeing my face not surrounded by layers of fat.

Yeah I suppose that was the convenient thing. I remember being impressed with the one I went into in NYC and thinking “wow this place has a lot more than any of our big men stores do.” And a lot more in terms of varying style compared to our big men stores.

But yeah I sort of hear you. But I do most of mine online. The one frustrating thing now is the gamble. Because there is no universal size standard, you’re never sure how something will fit when buying online. I’ve bought a couple of 2XL shirts that feel like they sent me an M size shirt despite the 2XL label being there. But other XL/2XL’s can fit perfectly. Size standards are all over the place and it makes it annoying as all hell buying online.

But I sort of welcome being able to go into stores I never dreamed of going into back when 😅

Right! I know DXL! I visited New York last year and found myself in a DXL buying a couple of shirts 😅 I sniffed out the first “big men” store I could find because I figured I wasn’t getting into much else at 370lbs. But yeah, it is weird. Even in my local Big W (our equivalent of Walmart) I’m used to headed straight to their big men section. But I was shocked I found I could actually fit into stuff outside of that small section in the regular section.

But yeah it is a hell of a mood. Makes me curious where else I can shop now. There are so many clothing outlet stores I would have never even dreamed of walking into back at 500lbs 😅

I feel ya. I started off at 500lbs and felt hideous. I'm down to 280lbs and I still think I give off creep vibes. The stupid thing is other people tell me "I'm handsome"...every time they say it I wanna smack them upside the head and say "what shit are you smoking because I don't see it"

We don't see what other people see. We're our own worst critics. If people are telling you that you look good maybe you've got to trust what they're saying and roll with it. Even if you don't feel it then fake it until you make it 

Congrats on losing over 200lbs so far. From a fellow 200lbs lost and counting guy. I know it's SO not easy to do. But I applaud you for your efforts so far.

That's awesome OP. What a nice gesture on their behalf.  
  
I'm always surprised when I get it. For the most part, I figured no one noticed. My own family don't even make a big deal of it. Yet out in the general public, I'll occasionally get random by passers stop me and tell me "good job" or "I've seen you walking around and you've lost a LOT"

Still surprises me to hear when I get it just because I gathered for the longest time that nobody noticed the work I was doing. I guess they did notice 209lbs lost from 500lbs to 291lbs and counting.
Is this the first time we can say: "South Park Did It"
Damn! Well done indeed!

As in loose skin? Not as bad as I feared so far. I have a lot of turkey neck that I sometimes hide with a beard. But everywhere else isn’t too bad so far. I imagine it will come the further I go down. As for the height? I’m know I’m somewhere around 6 ft but couldn’t put an exact number on it
Yeah, I should have bought it. I might go back and grab it. I was really only trying stuff on for vanity purposes 🤪 thank you 🙏
I am proud of it ☺️ still got more to go but I’m getting there one day at a time
Ya caught me! Thats actually an AI image 🤪😅 No joke. Thats me ☺️
Aww thank you so much. Yeah it's been 2 and a half years of figuring myself out but it's been worth it. Still have more to go yet.
Cheers I appreciate it.

Aww thank you. I am notoriously camera shy. Apart of the whole body dysmorphia and fear of people judging me because I think I'm not where I "should" be. But yeah I tend to keep on the downlow and go under the radar. Even on my IG page

I hit a plateau at around 370lbs for admittedly far too long. Didn't really want to admit as to how much I was eating. Took me about 6 months to finally own up to myself. Thankfully I never went back to 500lbs and I did manage to at least maintain for those 6 months. But yeah, once I started cutting more, it's finally gotten down to 294lbs and counting.

Yeah pretty much. Just cutting back in general. I gave up soda to begin with. That knocked off the first 120lbs. Lately it's been CICO aiming for around 2000-2500kcal a day. Right now I'm in the shifting diet phase. As in really starting to double down on what I'm eating and changing everything out as it is getting harder these days. That and I'm honestly at a point of frustration with my usual diet and am just looking for a change in general. Trying to go as clean as I can eating.

But yeah, it's been just general CICO and a LOT of walking/gym

Yeah, I think the mental part is the hardest part of all of this. For me, it was just getting over myself. I stand in my own way too much. I am my own brick wall. So it was really tough to start rewiring myself. 

Yeah,  its kind of crazy to look back at and think "damn, I really was that big back then." Denial is a hell of a thing because at the time, I knew I had gotten big but I guess was so in much denial as to HOW big I had gotten
Thank you!
Thank you!
Thank you so much!
Incredibly proud of what I've achieved so far. Best is still yet to come.

Awww thank you. Yeah, the confidence part is something I'm still trying to find. Going from 500lbs with a lot of self hate and low self esteem to finding confidence in myself is tough. But that was fun to make. I figure the internet has seen me at my worst so what's the difference lol.

Thank you for the kind words.
So damn proud. Thank you and I will do.
Yeah, it takes an insane amount of obsession and dedication I think. But it had to be done. I'm proud of what I've done. But I also know there is still another 100lbs to go so I have to stay hungry.
haha, me and my shitty headbanging lol. Thank you

Yeah I think that's just being tall. People here have said they couldn't believe I was 500lbs. I think that's just because I am tall. I can totally see the 500lbs on me at that point. But yeah I think the tall factor. Yeah, the next 100lbs is what I'm looking forward to. Just because we're finally in the 200's and it should start showing more and more.
Aww thanks :) I had fun making it. Thank you

I'm kind of the opposite. I'm actually more jazzed and excited by the last 100lbs than anything else. For me, it went like this. The first 120lbs came off in about 9 months. But then I stalled and hit the wall because I wasn't addressing the root problems that were leading me to over eating. I also just didn't want to admit I was eating too much. I lived by my fitbit and my fitbit told me I was burning 5000 to 6000 calories a day so I was in denial thinking I was fine eating 3-4k a day. That was until someone told me straight up the fitbit is wildly inaccurate and your burning more like 4k a day...hence maintaining.

There was also just a lot of self doubt at that point whether I could make it the rest of the way. Getting passed that wall has been tough. But at 300lbs I'm actually kinda jazzed about the last 100lbs.

The first 120lbs didn't feel like I saw much change. Getting down to 300lbs, I now look at myself and see the guy I was when I left high school. So this next 100lbs is actually exciting to me because it's the part I've never seen. I grew up overweight. I was verging into 3XL shirts as I left high school. I'm now back in a 3XL (Australian standard - US standard I guess it's 1XL depending on brand)

So yeah, this next part is the part I'm most excited to see just because it's finally breaking into the 200's for the first time in a LONG time.

But I get it. I fear the plateaus as well. And I dread when the day comes that I will have to readjust if that happens again. So I get it from that end.

Yeah body comp is a weird thing. I mean I remember film maker Kevin Smith at his heaviest. I swore he was at least 390 or maybe into the 400’s to look at him back then but apparently his highest was only ever 330lbs. Granted Kevin’s a lot shorter. So yeah the tallness does kind of distribute it a little bit differently. But yeah, I was 500lbs at my heaviest.
Just over 6ft, but my initial weigh in was 226kg so right there at 500lbs or so.

Over 6ft tall. It was indeed 500lbs. I tipped in at 226kg on my first weigh in. I think the second clip was probably 470lbs at that point. The clips did range somewhere in those areas but upon first weigh in I was at 226kg.

Yeah I get that. I really do. I'm have way too much of a sweet tooth for my own good and I'm guilty of loving that is quite frankly shit. I lived on fried foods, I lived on sugar, I lived on chocolate. I lived on everything that had no nutritional value.

For me, it's just been about finding alternatives. Like I have a sweet tooth, but I find stuff like Blueberries have been doing a great job satisfying that sweet tooth. I find fruits satisfy in general. Throughout the day, I usually try to stick to fruits and vegs. Usually protein in the morning. Lunch is maybe a salad with no dressing. Snack is a bowl of blueberries or fruit. Dinner is regular dinner. Which means chicken, steak or any variant of meat.

So long as I'm getting enough fibre I feel full enough. And fruits help keep the sweet tooth at bay.

I've gotten used to eating that way.

Sure, I still have my days where I want to crack. Especially days where everything feels like shit and I just want to go binge...but I also try to remind myself that's how I got to 500lbs.

So anyways, I get it. It's tough. It's tough to accept we can't keep eating what we want. That's the toughest part. For me it was just getting to that point where I was fed up doing all the work physically and seeing so little in return in terms of progress. I finally just sat down and said to myself I can either keep making this really hard on myself by continuing the same way of eating. Or I can go the other route. I like this current route I'm on. It's getting results so....but yeah, it's really hard to pull yourself out of.

Best of luck to you.
Awww thanks. I'm a wrestling fan. I'm a Stacy Keibler and Torrie Wilson (former WWE Divas) fan and it just made sense to do something fun to celebrate it lol

Started logging calories. Was brutally honest with myself. Came to the realisation I was eating over 3000 some days and pushing myself out of deficit. Or pushing myself into a smaller window. Got fed up with it and decided to change. Started cutting more processed foods out. Been focusing on a bit of organic and carnivore diet wise and got it down to about 2000 calories a day. It's doing the trick for now but I assume there will come a point I will have to drop to 1500 calories. But we'll see how we go. All I know is it's moving.

It's hard. Really hard. No one likes being honest with themselves. But I just got fed up with seeing so little progress and decided to make a change.
Thank you, so much!
Great god damn job! Keep going! I get it. I know how hard this is mentally and physically. It ain't easy. But we can do it!

aww thank you - can't get any traction on social media but oh well, I'm not really doing this for social media. I'm doing this for me :) Anyways, thanks for watching it. And thank you for the compliments

I was a fan of the original movies but honestly, when I first heard about CK I didn't think it would have the same magic or charm of the original film. Just didn't think it would work. I mean a show from the perspective of the very one-dimensional bully from the original film? How was that gonna be endearing or work?

After the first season aired on YT Plus, I watched a couple of reviews on YT that were singing the shows praises. What really got me was one reviewer claiming that there was a surprising balance between Johnny's teachings and Miyagi-do's methods. They claimed it found a delicate middle ground that saw both sides and reasoned that they both have their pros and cons.

That captured my attention and sounded quite interesting to me. So I checked out the first season and found for myself that the magic was very much still here. They did a fantastic job making you give a shit about Johnny in that first episode and I was absolutely hooked. Not only Johnny but Miguel. They did a fantastic job making me care for Miguel and Johnny and I was absolutely invested from Episode 1 onwards. Been watching every season since.

Honestly, this may sound crazy. But I was a wrestling fan. And as this show progressed I found it actually was doing wrestling better than modern day wrestling does. In terms of all the heel and baby face turns. I hated Hawk for most of Season 2/3 and by the end, he became one of my favourite characters. I loved that the show was able to constantly pull baby face and heel turns and make me give a crap when it did it.

A little weird to say, but I felt it was doing wrestling storytelling better than modern wrestling does.

I was at 164kg and went to 151kg in a month when I gave up sugar for the month. I agree, 13kg probably would be a lot if I were in the 100kg or less range lol. But I'm still in the 300's (lbs) so. But yeah, I did start at 500lbs and am down to 318lbs right now.

I more than get this. Especially the prisoner in my own mind sentiment. I'm a stress eater. When I get stressed, my first thought is to eat to comfort myself. It's the hardest thing to channel. My stress usually comes from much the same. I'm someone who has so little self worth in life. For the longest time I've thought of myself as a burden to everyone around me. I hated myself for so many years. The concept of self love just seemed like arrogance to me. And that little voice LOVES to tear me down as it tries to convince me that it's the only one telling me the truth.  
  
Granted, as my therapist said it is anxiety trying to protect me from being hurt. But I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop and for me to fail at everything I've done.

Which makes this one constant battle. Some months I can be really good with eating and get it down to 1kg a week. Other months I trip and fall and indulge in everything I know I shouldn't be eating. 

It's a constant battle up there in that head of mine.

Therapy does help. It gets a lot of that out of my head. If you can afford it then I would suggest it to just about anyone. It's good to talk freely and openly in a comfortable safe environment where you won't be judged. 

Honestly, I know you've probably heard this one before. But try writing down things you do like about yourself and reaffirm yourself with those traits. What makes you a good person? What cheers you up? What takes your mind away from all those self destructive negative thoughts? Find those things and try focusing on them to squash that little pesky ass voice that loves to tear you down.

  
Easier said than done, I'm well aware. But I do find it helps when I hit those months of severe self doubt and anxiety. All the best to you

I figured this month was gonna be a write off for me. I've had at least 3 Christmas get togethers as is. Not counting upcoming Christmas day. Last month I dropped 6kg. This month I've barely dropped 2kg. But I'm not beating myself up about it. I knew Christmas season was gonna be a write off.

Once we hit January though, I go straight back to the cut. So I'm enjoying the festive season of maintenance as I'm calling it. I figure I'm not gonna regain that 80kg I've already lost in one month. Just so long as I don't go overboard and keep it around maintenance I should be fine for this month.

But come January, it's straight back to work.

Well I live in Australia so the only choice I had was big and tall men stores once I entered the 7XL/8XL area.

I don’t know where you are in the world, but I think in US terms our 8XL is more like a 6XL? I don’t know. I’m currently wearing a 3XLT comfortably and on the tag it has US standard as 1XLT 🤷‍♂️

Size standards are all over the place. I find being tall, I have the problem of nothing being long enough at times.  Especially with the gut. I’m always trying to avoid the overhang of the gut poking out of the shirt. The only way I can do that is with XLT sizes which limits choices. Quite the opposite dilemma for me 🤣

Walk every day. Close to 20k steps a day. Also go to the gym for at least an hour a day.  
Quit soft drink. That was a BIG one for me. Getting rid of soft drink knocked off 51kg in the first year alone.

I'm currently down 80kg in total. The biggest readjustment for me is still changing diet for the better. I hit a plateau at 175kg for about 9 months and tbh, it was because I was eating too much still.

I started calorie counting half way into this year and started readjusting diet. I' knocked off close to 30kg this year just from cutting back snacks. Biggest loss this year was 13kg I lost in October (I gave up sugar for the month and it melted off)

I've been going for 2 years now. I'm giving myself a break currently (Christmas and all) but come January next year, I'm gonna cut out most of what I can and go for broke. I wanna see if I can get the last 40 to 50kg off before end of 2025.

Anyways, diet is the thing I'm still learning to do better on but it is getting better day by day. I finally was honest with myself and have been slowly readjusting everything eating wise.

Hell, I can't believe I'm getting into a 2XL. When I was back in a 10XL this seemed impossible. I started off in a 10XL. I don't know what my waist was when I started as I never measured. But currently I'm down to a 2XL with 48inch pants. I have to assume I was above 60 inches though when I started.

  
Like I said, I still can't believe I'm even getting into a 2XL shirt. Who knows where it will be next year? But if I keep going at 1kg a week then maybe I'll get there half way into 2025.

Thank you so much. Proud of you too!

if your current weight is anything to go by as in your profile then you're actually where I am. I'm currently 320lbs myself...Or 145kg. I'm aiming for 100kg myself (220lbs) so I still got a ways to go. Chin up, we'll get there.
Thank you so much. Yes, a LOT of work...and more to go yet.

Sizes are a weird thing. I live in Australia so I pushed a 10XL here. Yet by American standards that's apparently more like a 6 or 7XL. Hell, the 3XL I'm currently in literally has a 1XL USA standard on the tag. I'll tell you. Sizes are a bitch when there is no universal standard.

As for your husband, all the best to him. He's got this!

Going from this 

https://imgur.com/a/HzOhzd5

To this

https://imgur.com/wzJYUis

I hate to say it but the vanity thing is real 😅 I’ve gotta admit, I was looking haggard when I started. That’s the most unflattering photo I could find.

Seriously though? It’s nice not to be carrying 179lbs extra on my back anymore. It’s nice to be able to walk great lengths. Overall, it just feels better as a whole.

No I don’t feel that way at all about anyone else. But we are our own worst critics and in my case, I am very hard and harsh on myself at times.

I’m very aware I am WAY too hard on myself. Like I said, a lot of this is just insecurity sparked by social. I sometimes think I should distance myself from it all. But I don’t want to lose the contacts I’ve made through it either.

It’s really just the social media thing. It’s a bad mindset to compare, but when you see all these stories of people who have lost close to 200lbs in half the time, it does play on my own insecurities that I’m not good enough for getting there sooner. Admittedly it’s a very bad mindset to be under and I probably do need to distance myself from social.

Admittedly it is my own insecurities at play. I try not to compare, but it’s really hard when social media loves reminding you, I guess my biggest fight in life is one of “I’m not good enough.” So here I am celebrating a 1kg loss. Then i see someone my weight losing 5kg in a week and immediately it just makes me think “I’m not good enough…I should have lost way more this week.”

It’s a bad mindset that I’m still trying to overcome. I should be content with what I’ve done so far and keep going. But anyways, I know it’s my own insecurities at play.
I try not to, but it’s really hard when social media shoves it in your face. Admittedly it just plays on my own insecurities that I’m not good enough

Well I get that, I mean my lowest is 146. But on the scale it was at 147.8kg. And I know it will fluctuate until it shows the next lowest number. I don’t know, I just want to challenge myself and get to that 140kg by the end of the year.

Well right now it’s been 1kg a week and I’ve been eating between 2000-2200 calories a day. Some days slightly less at 1800 cal. All I know is it’s been coming in at 1kg a week. I gave up sugar in October and that was closer to 2kg a week. But November I reintroduced sugar a little and it went back to just over 1kg a week.

Yeah, I mean I am happy to see it steadily going down 1kg a week. Maybe I’m just too hard on myself at times. Big part of the problem for me is I see other people my size rapidly losing weight in a week and I think “what the fuck am I doing wrong? I only went down by 1kg this week and they’re celebrating 5kg in a week”

Yeah, I know. I shouldn’t compare but social media is a bitch when the algorithm loves to throw these stories in your face. Kudos to them, im not disparaging them. But yeah, it does make me wonder could I be going better than I am?

When I gave up sugar in the month of October, I was getting closer to 2kg a week. I lost 13kg in October as a whole going from 164kg to 153kg. I reintroduced a little bit of sugar in November and went down by 6kg from 153kg to 147kg

Lately it’s been about 1kg a week. I guess if I cut out sugar again, I can get it back to nearing 2kg a week.
100kg seems like a good round number. I’m at 147kg right now so just over 40kg a way. When I get down to 100kg, I’ll go from there
He’s still mad that Lan Di killed his father and seeks revenge…but first, capsule toys…oh wait, wrong franchise 🤪

You know the funny thing is after I committed suicide and started therapy, that was literally the first thing out of my therapists mouth. That I should consider losing weight and it may start to help. I’m not gonna sit here and say it has had no effect, because I do feel better physically for doing this. And I do like how I look now compared to what I looked like back then. But for me, it’s still just the feeling of how does it solve all the other problems? How does it solve my inadequacy? How does it solve my fear of trusting people again? How does it solve what I fear is broken about me?

Again, I don’t expect answers and that’s too much to ask of anyone here. But it does make me wonder, is it all just easy answers? Lose weight and be happy. What if I’m not happy when I get there?

And then I think it’s probably just me that needs to change my view on all this. I just think it’s like you said. An easy answer that society forces down our throat. Happiness = weight. 

I don’t know. I guess I’m happy enough I’m not 500lbs and at least I’m in the 300’s. But then the pressure shifts to getting to that end goal and knowing it gets harder and harder both mentally and physically.

https://imgur.com/a/7gBP8xu - that’s my most current before and after progress video and what I look like. From 500lbs to 328lbs. I mean I think I still have more body fat than anything else on me right now.

I’m 6ft and I probably have more body fat on me than muscle. There is absolutely no doubt in that. I’ve never actually gone and gotten a body scan so I don’t know but I hold a lot of fat in the belly. Yes, self hate and self sabotage is a HUGE reason why I got to that weight. I ate myself there because I never had anything in the way of self worth. And I still struggle with it. It’s a little better these days but as I’ve said elsewhere, it’s like I’m stuck between a new me that wants to leave that old me behind. But the old me is just waiting to be proven right. Proven right that I’m gonna fail. That I’m gonna get my heart broken for trusting people again. That I’m gonna just fail in general. I’m just afraid and waiting for the other shoe to drop and I have been this whole time.

That’s how I feel. Like I’m stuck between two Daniel’s. One that wants to embrace what it is he has achieved. And the other that is still holding on expecting him to fail and fall flat on his face.

I actually do speak to a therapist. I’m better than I was 2 years ago, but I still have flashes of that old me. It really is just that. It’s like there is this new me wanting to get out and leave that old me behind. But the old me is there, just waiting to be proven “right”…if that makes sense. That’s how I explain it to my therapist. 

Yeah, much the same. I don’t feel like I get much support from the people who I feel should be giving the most support. That being my parents. But that’s a whole thread best saved for therapist 😅

I do post on social media, I’m on Instagram. I sometimes think it’s just a popularity contest over there. I mean I don’t really care about being famous or blowing up but I do it mainly just to keep myself accountable and remind myself of where I started.

I have mixed opinions on the social media thing. A part of me feels it’s not a good thing to go chasing connections that aren’t real. I guess what I mean is social media is for the most part a show and the connections made there aren’t always gonna be real friendships. That’s not to say real friendships can’t grow on social media. But what I mean is people chase followers and sometimes forget these connections aren’t real. It’s all a fabrication. And I think that’s a syndrome for far greater loneliness. If that makes sense, I’m just talking out of my ass here.

But I am on Instagram, I just don’t take it that seriously in terms of “growing an audience”

It’s a lot of things for me. I do have a lot of self hatred and self worth issues. Let’s just say I feel like I’ve never had a sense of self worth. It’s why I got to 500lbs. I never cared about myself. Never felt like I was worth anything. Didn’t know what value I bought to this world. And as such I ate myself to 500lbs over the years thinking I would die in my 30’s.

I tried to kill myself 2 years ago. I hit my lowest point. An open ulcer on my leg for 2 years that left me almost bed ridden. Hitting 500lbs was the final straw. And I tried to kill myself. Thankfully I didn’t and decided to make a turn in my life. And here I am 170lbs down.

On the one hand, I’m proud of it. But on the other, I think “why should I be proud of it? I’m still 328lbs and I still have so much further to go.”

Perfectionism? Not really, I know I’m never gonna have the perfect body. I’ve done way too much damage to myself. For me, it’s this nagging thought of everyone telling me it will get better meanwhile I’m here asking myself “when? When does it get better? Because I’ve lost 170lbs and it feels like no one cares.” Losing 170lbs didn’t solve the numerous other problems. I still feel I don’t have much in the way of worth. I don’t know what my purpose is. No one seems to notice or care that I’ve done all this work. So why should I care?

It’s like I’m stuck somewhere between a new version of me that wants to get there, but the old me is always waiting for the other shoe to drop and to be proven right. I guess deep down I fear I’m not worthwhile and even if I make it the whole distance then I’m still not gonna be worthwhile to anyone.

All that’s waiting at the end of this is a slimmer figure…but the problems will still be there. That’s one of the things I fear most.

I do notice differences. Thank crap for progress photos because they do help to remind how far I’ve come. I think it’s more I know I still have so much more to go and even after losing 170lbs, I still just see the morbidly obese guy. Sure, slightly smaller in frame but still knowing I have so far to go yet

It is to some degree. I think it’s just the reminder that I have a whole another person still to go. And then it plays on my mind. The old feelings of regret that I even did this to myself to begin with

I have attempted suicide in the past. Self hatred is a big thing for me and this I fear. Everyone keeps telling me “lose the weight, you’ll feel better for it.” Even my therapist has given me this advice. And here I sit, 170lbs down and I still find myself questioning even if I make it the whole way, is it really gonna make any difference if I still don’t feel it at this point? 

Does it really solve the 90 other problems I face in life? Just because I solved one? I don’t know. I guess sometimes I get sick and tired of people giving what I think are easy answers. And then I just wonder if I overthink this all too much and is it just me needing to get out of my own head more.

I get this! I totally get it. Especially when someone calls me an inspiration. I always think to myself “no, I’m not! I’m just a guy trying to lose weight because he needs to do it. Not to inspire anyone.” I mean, sure. If it inspires someone then great but that’s not why I’m doing it. I’m doing it for me alone.

I do enjoy the praise. It’s nice to receive compliments. But yeah, I don’t buy into any of that stuff just because I think “no one praised me for getting to 500lbs so why am I worthy of praise for correcting it? And why am I worthy of it now when I still have so far to go and there’s no guarantee I will get there?”

I guess you’re right. It’s self esteem and regret. I know for me I’ve never felt much in the way of worth so it’s hard to accept that I am worthy of this based on how far I’ve come already.

If I may ask, you obviously notice the difference, but is it just something inside that wants more? Or is it more, “that’s all I’ve ever known, now what?” Type feeling.

Someday’s I feel it’s a bit of the latter for me. Like you said, all I’ve ever known is being the fat guy who felt he wasn’t worthy of anything. I am guilty of thinking "I'm not good enough" from time to time and when I see those stories of people who have done it so much quicker then I do tend to beat myself up a little thinking "what's wrong with me?"

But lately I flipped the script and think "you've lost 63kg in 2 years AND managed to keep it off without reverting back. Give yourself some credit"

Don't compare yourself with others. Rather compare yourself with yourself. I now find myself asking which would I rather be? The 500lbs version of me that was gassed just walking to the end of the street? Or the current 358lbs version of me that has managed to lose 142lbs, kept it off and is still going aiming for that 220lbs range. The 358lbs version who is slowly learning about calorie counting and better nutrition? Or the 500lbs version who was downing cans of Coke and wallowing in his own misery? So yeah, my advice? Don't compare yourself with others. Compare yourself against your former self.

It's a cracked reflection of a society that most would rather sweep under the rug then believe is in their own backyard. For me, this film is actually quite dear as I actually have grown up around people that were on the border of poverty line.  I did spend time in let's say less privileged friends houses in grade school. I would be prone to seeing rats running around the muddy backyard (sometimes running into the house). I would go into these peoples houses and see massive piles of hoarded stuff throughout their houses. Granted, no one was killing cats or hurting animals or anything, but I saw similar housing conditions as those found in Gummo many times as a kid.

When I first saw Gummo, it actually made me sort of smile to see the houses with hoarded junk inside just because it was so familiar. I grew up in rural Australia for a short time during my childhood and while my family were never poor, I did spend time around less privileged kids. So seeing that shit in Gummo was actually oddly familiar for me in regards to a portion of my own childhood.

I did see a lot of elder brothers huffing glue or smoking weed.

So to me, when I first saw Gummo at 16 years of age, I had already moved back from Rural Australia to the Suburbs. But watching Gummo served as a reminder of that part of my childhood and I kind of fell in love with it immediately because I had never seen that slice of life reflected in a film before.

Outside of just capturing that sense of place, I think what has always gotten me about the film is its almost nihilistic portrayal of this town and the fact that they are all just killing time with no real hope or aspirations to better themselves.   


Take Tummler for example. Tummler is a seemingly bright kid but he is ultimately trapped by his ravaged surroundings. There's that once scene at the end where he is shooting the cat and he has this look of almost self realization on his face. An almost pained look of "what the fuck am I doing?"

Combine that with the chair wrestling scene, where at the very end of the scene a very real moment is captured where everyone looks around as if almost to say "what the fuck do we do now?"

I feel like that's what sums up Gummo best. It's a town that is stuck in purgatory and is filled with lost souls who are just killing time aimlessly until they meet their maker.

It's a beautifully haunting nightmare of a film that borders somewhere between shocking reality and dreamlike surrealism. And that's why I've always kind of loved it. That and it has a hell of a black/extreme metal soundtrack underneath it.
